    Docs / BenchmarksSource: docs/benchmarks.md

    Reproducing performance evidence

    tests/benchmark/budget.sh gates CI and releases: a fixed representative configuration is timed against an empty shell on macOS and Linux. It tests loaded state before timing, uses interleaved runs, and reports the difference of medians. This is a regression budget, not a competitor ranking.

    tests/benchmark/compare.sh compares actual pinned managers using zsh-bench. Each setup has the same 20 aliases, 10 PATH entries, 5 constants, completion system and two pinned plugins, with the same minimal prompt. Wayu's built-in suggestions/highlighting and deferred modes are separate configurations.

    Run after building wayu and downloading the pinned Sheldon binary through the ecosystem fetcher (or supply an installed executable):

    SHELDON_BIN=/tmp/wayu-upstreams/bin/sheldon \
ONLY="floor plain wayu oh-my-zsh antidote sheldon sheldon-static" \
ITERS=32 JSON=/tmp/wayu-comparison.json tests/benchmark/compare.sh

    Sheldon is measured both with its normal eval "$(sheldon source)" startup and with a pre-generated static loader. The latter must be regenerated when its configuration changes. These are separate rows, not interchangeable results. The optional optimize scenario uses simulated slow completion generators; it is not a measurement of real kubectl, gh or helm startup.

    What the report records#

    • Warmed PTY measurements: first prompt, first command, command/input lag and process exit; every raw sample and the median of each metric.
    • Detected completion/suggestion/highlighting flags, so missing or deferred work is visible. Do not compare a deferred first prompt with fully loaded startup as if the same work had finished. The upstream detector may not recognize wayu's native features; inspect the named configuration as well as the detector flags for those rows.
    • One first-process-exit observation for each fresh HOME after setup. Generated artifacts may already exist; this diagnostic is neither a cold first-prompt latency nor a statistically reliable median.
    • UTC date, platform/architecture, shell version, wayu version and binary hash, source commit/dirty state, tool/source pins and cache state.

    The JSON writer rejects incomplete or non-finite timing samples. The scheduled and manually triggered ecosystem workflow retains JSON, human-readable output and the checksum manifest for macOS and Linux. Reports from different machines should be compared as separate experiments; cloud-runner noise and hardware differences do not support a universal speed claim.

    Use at least 32 iterations for a report you publish, repeat the experiment, and report distributions and feature flags. Shorter runs are tooling smoke checks. zsh-bench requires PTY support; a machine unable to allocate a PTY cannot supply this evidence. Keep failed runs as failures rather than replacing them with plain zsh -c exit results.

    The upstream measurement tool is zsh-bench. See the pinned revisions and workload in the script. Performance evidence is separate from compatibility checks and from an independent security review.
